source.title: FIT to Forget: Robust Continual Unlearning for Large Language Models
source.authors: XiaoYu Xu; Min-Xin Du; Kun Fang; Ya-Xin Xiao; Zhi-Cong Huang; Cheng Hong; Qing-Qing Ye; Hai-Bo Hu

record.tranche_reason: Tests relearning and quantization recovery using a continual-unlearning framework and F.D. metric, rather than the recovery methods and measures of the original studies.
record.gate_note: Figure 7 reports F.D. for ten unlearning methods before and after three relearning settings and int4 quantization. The paper's text summarizes only some method groups and FIT; the plotted values cannot be assigned reliably from the supplied figure extraction, so those values are recorded as figure only. Table 2's F.D./R.U. results assess continual unlearning but do not directly report targeted accuracy relative to chance.
record.test_reason: Section 5.2 and Figure 7 run relearning attacks (mixed, retain-only and unrelated data) and int4 quantization on ten unlearned Llama-3-8B models, including the authors' FIT. The measure differs from the originals: F.D. is a symmetric closeness-to-retain-model score, not target accuracy against chance. The recovery results bear on B, D and F.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that FIT gives the best forgetting-utility trade-off under continual unlearning and better resists relearning and int4 quantization recovery. The robustness claim is relative (highest F.D. after mixed relearning and int4; only competitive for retain-only and unrelated-only relearning) and is shown only on Llama-3-8B.
record.recipe_differences: FIT combines redundancy filtering, importance-guided selection among unlearning algorithms, and targeted layer updates for continual requests; it evaluates relearning and int4 recovery attacks rather than reproducing an original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery is evaluated on Llama-3-8B under mixed, retain-only, or unrelated-only relearning and int4 quantization. The text describes FIT's relative result as strongest for mixed relearning and quantization, and competitive for the other two data conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Sequential (continual) application of standard unlearning methods drives GA, GA+KL, RLabel and PISCES to collapse (F.D./R.U. 0, GSM8K 0 on Llama-3-8B after 300 requests).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continual unlearning causes catastrophic utility collapse for standard methods.

record.problems: Recovery outcomes are presented in Figure 7 without assignable numeric values in the supplied text extraction. The recovery evaluation is reported for Llama-3-8B; the tested relearning does not include access to forgotten facts, and quantization is limited to int4. The paper notes that its synthetic proxy retain models may not perfectly match true retraining behavior.

untested.parts: Target accuracy relative to chance is never reported. The F.D. metric treats over-forgetting as failure, which does not map onto A's near-chance criterion.
Relearning on a subset of the forgotten facts or the forget set is explicitly excluded. Only Llama-3-8B is attacked.
Entirely untested: no activation ablation and no access-vs-deletion analysis.
Only int4 on Llama-3-8B; no other bit widths or quantization schemes.
Entirely untested: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attacks.
FIT is not tested against internal-edit or prompting attacks, nor on models other than Llama-3-8B for robustness.

missing.what: Pre-attack F.D. for each method on Llama-3-8B after 300 requests (e.g., FIT 0.73, ALKN 0.60, O3 0.64, NPO+KL 0.59, GA 0.00), needed as the baseline for the Figure 7 attack rows
Partially extracted Figure 7 bar labels (e.g., 0.10, 0.12, 0.11, many 0.00) that cannot be assigned to methods; these should be re-read from the figure image

record.verdict_notes: F.D. = max(0, 1−|F/FQ−1|) penalises both under- and over-forgetting. A low F.D. after an attack can mean either recovery or continued collapse, so it is a weak proxy for recovery. The baselines GA, GA+KL, RLabel and PISCES are already collapsed before any attack, so their attack rows say nothing about B or D. No labels are given for B or D because no row value is readable and the measure cannot isolate recovery. The D.3 statement that PISCES 'exhibits substantial recoverability' cites prior work and is not a result of this study.

versions.untested_parts: Recovery resistance is evaluated, but the paper does not establish that targeted-knowledge accuracy is near chance or directly compare it with chance. Downstream capability is evaluated separately, not as part of the recovery attack conditions.
Tests mixed retain/unrelated data, retain-only data, and unrelated-only data; does not test relearning with a subset of forgotten facts or the forget set.
No activation-direction ablation to restore knowledge, nor an experiment establishing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests int4 weight quantization only; does not test other bit widths or quantization schemes.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context-information recovery test.
FIT is evaluated against relearning and int4 quantization only; it is not tested against internal-edit or prompting attacks.

tranche.reason: FIT is a different method on the same question, tested with relearning and int4 attacks.

source_check.notes: Robustness is relative to the other methods, on Llama-3-8B only, with figure-only values. The bar labels in the extracted text (0.00-0.12) can't be assigned to bars. Retain-only and unrelated-only relearning are only called competitive. Relearning uses no forget-set data. F.D. is symmetric closeness to the retain model.

statements.correction: FIT: Llama-3-8B, PCH benchmark, ten methods compared. Relearning uses mixed retain/unrelated data, with no forget-set data. Text says FIT has the highest F.D. after mixed relearning and is only competitive under retain-only and unrelated-only relearning. Values are figure-only. F.D. measures closeness to the retain model, not forget accuracy. Preprint, one model.
statements.problem: Cites R01 but says nothing about FIT. Its conditions (1B-3B Llama/Qwen plus Zephyr; TOFU, LKF, FaithUn, WMDP-cyber; forget-set or disjoint QA fine-tuning) and its 'why' do not cover FIT's setting. R01 is figure-only (cannot_determine), so FIT backs none of the listed numbers.

statements.correction: FIT: Llama-3-8B on PCH, int4 quantization of the unlearned weights. Text says FIT has the highest F.D. among ten methods after int4. Value is figure-only, with no numeric before/after against the unlearned bar. Preprint, one model.
statements.problem: Cites R04 but names no FIT result. The benchmarks listed (WMDP and MUSE) and the 'why' leave out FIT and its PCH benchmark. R04 is figure-only (cannot_determine).
none; Figure 7 runs relearning (mix, retain, unrel.) and INT4 quantization as separate settings on Llama-3-8B, with no combined attack
